observations.notes: The chip load band is printed; the family assignment is not (row_kind derived, grade b, by the R5 rule for a shared column). One 'Wood' row for all wood. The tool is a brad-point / through-hole boring bit, NOT a router end mill: this row must not serve an EndMill plunge. The sheet prints no peck or hole-depth guidance.

observations.source_title: PreciseBits Hardwood Fingerboard Planing and Radiusing 3-flute up-cut end mills (product page)
observations.source_page: product page 'Application Data', Plunge rate (based on wood hardness)
observations.material_label: wood by Janka (PreciseBits fingerboard page)
observations.verbatim: Plunge rate (based on wood hardness): ... Softwood (Janka < 1,500) = 75 inches/minute ... Tip Radius (R) = 0.0250 inches (0.64mm)
observations.notes: Printed plunge FEED RATE 75 IPM = 1905 mm/min for one tool: a 3-flute radiused (bull-nose) end mill, D 0.125 in / 3.0 mm, tip radius 0.64 mm. No RPM is printed ('for bits this small, use your maximum RPM'), so no plunge chip load follows without an assumed RPM; chipload fields are null. The page bands by Janka, not by softwood/hardwood: this row serves the printed band 'Softwood (Janka < 1,500) = 75 inches/minute'. hardness_value 600.0 is the engine's Janka proxy (GenericSoftwood 600, GenericHardwood 1450) or a point inside the printed band (2000 for 1,500-2,500; 2600 for > 2,500). The engine's generic hardwood (1450) falls in the < 1,500 band, so it reads 75 in/min, not 50. Vendor page for one application (fingerboard planing): grade b.

verdicts.note: Live HTML prints 'Softwood (Janka < 1,500) = 75 inches/minute'. 1905 mm/min correct. No RPM, so the chip load is null. hardness_value 600 is an engine proxy inside the printed band.
